components.cost_effect: One subgradient call, one update Exp and one projection per step.
components.goal: Take a tangent descent step while retaining feasibility.
components.name: Projected exponential step
components.operation: Query g_s, evaluate Exp_{x_s}(-eta g_s), then apply the exact nearest-point projection onto X.
components.requires: Hadamard geometry, exact operations and the closed geodesically convex set.
transfer_checks: A retraction or approximate projection requires a new error analysis.
Curvature lower bounds and nonexpansive projection must remain valid.

components.cost_effect: t-1 extra Log and t-1 extra Exp evaluations for the returned average.
components.goal: Convert the mean of iterate objective values into a feasible output guarantee.
components.key_estimate: f(bar x_t)<=t^(-1)sum_{s=1}^t f(x_s); the complete elementary induction is separated in the linked Theorem record.
components.name: Recursive geodesic averaging
components.operation: Initialize bar x_1=x_1; interpolate from bar x_s toward x_{s+1} by fraction 1/(s+1).
components.requires: Unique connecting geodesics and geodesic convexity of both X and f.
transfer_checks: Ambient arithmetic averaging is not justified on a general manifold.
Changing the interpolation weights changes the Proof obligation.

content.family: Projected Riemannian subgradient with distance-potential analysis

limitations.statement: Needs public parameter bounds and a known horizon for the displayed constant step size; the theorem's guarantee applies to the recursive geodesic average.

variants.cost: Separately count t subgradient calls, t update Exp calls and t exact projections, plus t-1 Log calls and t-1 averaging Exp calls to construct bar x_t. Tangent scaling and maintaining state also require computation. The source does not provide arithmetic, dimension-dependent or projection implementation costs; none of these primitives is declared free.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Source PDF p.6 Eq. (2); p.9 Theorem 9 averaging and step-size formulas; p.10 Proof completion.
variants.name: Theorem 9 deterministic horizon-tuned variant
variants.output: Return bar x_t, the recursive geodesic average of x_1,...,x_t. The final update to x_{t+1} is present in the source Proof's t-step convention; it is not included in this average.
public_inputs: Hadamard manifold M and nonempty closed geodesically convex X
Positive diameter bound D and Lipschitz bound L_f
Exact subgradient, projection, Exp and Log capabilities
variants.query_and_update: For s=1,...,t query g_s at x_s and compute y_{s+1}=Exp_{x_s}(-eta g_s), x_{s+1}=P_X(y_{s+1}). For s<t compute bar x_{s+1}=Exp_{bar x_s}((1/(s+1))Log_{bar x_s}(x_{s+1})). No function-value query is needed for this prescribed update or output.
variants.requirements: M is Hadamard with sectional curvature in [kappa,0]; diam(X)<=D. f:M->R is geodesically convex and globally L_f-Lipschitz under Definitions 1/3, with an attained minimizer in X. Query returns g_s in T_{x_s}M satisfying the global tangent supporting inequality; these subgradients have norm at most L_f. P_X is the exact nearest-point projection. Performance conditions are fully recorded in thm.P102.nonsmooth_bound.
variants.state_and_initialization: Initialize x_1 in X and bar x_1=x_1. Maintain the current iterate and recursive average. Let zeta(kappa,D)=sqrt(|kappa|)D/tanh(sqrt(|kappa|)D), continuously extended to 1 at kappa=0.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use eta=D/(L_f sqrt(zeta(kappa,D)t)) throughout this run. Stop after the prescribed t queried steps. No adaptive stopping, line search or restart is specified by this variant.
